utility.notes: KIUC is a genuinely distinct entity from the Hawaiian Electric Industries family (which owns HECO/MECO/HELCO) — it is a member-owned, not-for-profit electric cooperative and the only one of its kind in Hawaii, confirmed via both KIUC's own site and the Hawaii PUC's own page listing it as a separate PUC-regulated electric utility. Its interconnection rules (Schedule Q, its own Tariff No. 2 'Distributed Generation Interconnection Policies and Procedures') are entirely separate from Hawaiian Electric's Smart DER framework and must not be assumed to follow the same terms.

value.name: Kauai Island Utility Cooperative (KIUC)
value.notes: Per KIUC's own 'Rooftop Solar' page: customers must submit an interconnection request application for engineering review before installing a system (required by Hawaii PUC rules). KIUC's own compensation mechanism for exported PV energy is governed by 'Tariff No. 1, Schedule Q Modified — Purchase from Qualified Facilities 100 kW or less,' distinct from HECO/MECO/HELCO's NEM/Smart DER programs. KIUC also curtails (temporarily limits) Schedule Q customer exports at times, per its own published Curtailment FAQ — a distinct, KIUC-specific operational reality not present in the Smart DER islands' documentation reviewed this session.

city.notes: Kauai County covers the entire island of Kaua'i (and Ni'ihau) under a single county government, not separate incorporated municipalities. This record represents the county-wide AHJ; per the mission's Hawaii-specific instruction, no separate sub-county city pages are created beneath it. 'Lihue' (the County seat and Building Division's own address) is used as the representative city identifier.

permit_authority.value: County of Kaua'i Department of Public Works, Building Division

required_documents.notes: The County's own solar-specific permitting document (Kauai County Chapter 12 Building Code's 'Solar Permits' provision, and a State Energy Office-hosted 'Residential Photovoltaic Systems' guide summarizing the County's process) were both blocked this session: the Chapter 12 PDF triggered a file-download dialog in the browser and returned HTTP 403 via WebFetch; the energy.hawaii.gov mirror returned a Cloudflare challenge via browser and HTTP 403 via WebFetch. A search-result snippet indicated Kauai issues a single combined 'solar permit' covering building/electrical/plumbing code requirements, but per the rule against using snippets as evidence, this was not recorded as a sourced fact — only the County's general Building Permit Guide (loaded directly) was used.

other_conditions: KIUC uses two distinct interconnection application forms depending on system size: one for systems less than 10 kW, and a separate one for systems greater than 10 kW
Customers must submit and receive engineering review approval of an interconnection request application before installing a PV system, per Hawaii PUC rules
